request: Meetings with government officials should be logged automatically so we stop losing engagement history.
executive_summary: This release will implement an automatic logging feature for meetings with government officials in the Government CRM, designed primarily for regional coordinators and project managers. Key features include ensuring user input for logging and establishing access protocols to maintain confidentiality. However, human decisions are still needed regarding organizational policies for handling unlogged meetings and access permissions when users leave or change roles.

core_commitments.text: Automatically log meetings with government officials, including details such as participants, date, and notes.
core_commitments.note: This feature is imperative to enhance the logging of meetings with government officials to prevent loss of engagement history.

core_commitments.text: Allow users to view and retrieve logged meeting histories easily.
core_commitments.note: Facilitating easy access to logged meeting histories is crucial for users to refer back to previous engagements.

in_scope.text: The system will log meetings when a user inputs the meeting details through an interface, specifying participants, date, and notes; an option for users to review and edit details for accuracy will be available before final submission.
in_scope.note: This approach ensures that users actively enter meeting details, reducing the risk of losing information due to missed inputs.

in_scope.text: Regional coordinators and project managers will have access to their own meeting logs, while access to meeting logs from other projects and regions will be limited to users with designated roles, such as senior management or authorized officers, as defined by the organization's data protection policy.
in_scope.note: Defining access rights to meeting logs is essential to protect sensitive data, as highlighted during the discussion on confidentiality.

in_scope.text: Users will receive a notification confirming that the meeting has been logged.
in_scope.note: Notifications confirm that meetings are logged adequately, helping users keep track of their engagement activities.

in_scope.text: Meeting log entries will be available for review in a timeline format within the CRM.
in_scope.note: The timeline format for review aids in providing a clear view of engagement activities to users.

in_scope.text: In the event a user leaves the organization suddenly and fails to log meeting details, a process will be established whereby an authorized user, designated by management, will be responsible for reaching out to the departing user or relevant team members to attempt to capture any unlogged meeting details before the user’s departure. If those details cannot be recovered, it will be documented as an exception in that user’s engagement history.
in_scope.note: This process establishes measures to address unlogged details when a user departs, ensuring that efforts are made to capture necessary information.

in_scope.text: If a user changes roles within the organization, their previous meeting logs will remain accessible to individuals in the user's new role if that role entails similar responsibilities, ensuring continuity in project engagement. Access permissions will be reviewed to ensure alignment with the organization's data protection policy.
in_scope.note: Maintaining access to previous meeting logs when users change roles guarantees continuity and minimizes disruption in engagement.

out_of_scope.text: The release will not include integration with external calendar applications for automatic meeting detection.
The release will not include analytics or reporting features on meeting data.
The release will not address logging meetings with non-government officials.

assumptions.text: Users have the necessary permissions to log meetings within the CRM, determining access to engagement histories.
assumptions.note: This assumption underscores the importance of established user permissions for effective logging within the CRM.

assumptions.text: The CRM already possesses a basic structure to log user input for meetings.
assumptions.note: It is presumed that the foundation for logging meetings is already in place within the CRM system.

assumptions.text: Users are willing to manually input meeting details at least once to trigger the logging process.
assumptions.note: User willingness to manually input meeting details is necessary to initiate the logging process.

definitions.text: "meetings with government officials" means scheduled interactions between CRM users and representatives from governmental entities, including but not limited to country representatives and ministry contacts.
definitions.note: Clarification of what constitutes 'meetings with government officials' aids in defining the logging parameters accurately.

definitions.text: "logged automatically" means that once users submit the required meeting details through the initial input interface, the system captures and stores this information without further action needed from the user; however, users must always provide those details and confirm submission to complete the logging process.
definitions.note: The revision ensures that users must still provide initial input for logging, addressing previous ambiguities around the logging process.

definitions.text: "engagement history" means the record of all interactions logged in the CRM, which includes meetings, contact details, and communications with government representatives, while sensitive meeting notes must be designated and encrypted to ensure access is restricted only to authorized personnel.
definitions.note: The definition of engagement history includes specifications on how sensitive information must be handled and encrypted.

success_criteria.text: At least 90% of logged meeting entries are successfully recorded without errors in the first month after deployment, measured by user reports and system logs.
success_criteria.note: Setting a benchmark for error-free logging of meetings ensures accountability and attention to data quality post-launch.

open_questions.question: What organizational policies are needed to guide the management of meeting logs when users leave suddenly, especially regarding unlogged details?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This policy is critical to ensure that engagement history is preserved even when a user departs unexpectedly.
options: Establish a formal procedure for capturing unlogged details before departure
Accept the risk of lost engagement history without defined policies

proposer.text: The management of meeting details for departing users depends on organizational policy and procedures, which must be defined by the organization itself. This includes what happens to records if meeting details are not input before a user leaves.

critic.text: What happens to meeting records when users leave is dependent on organizational policies that are not specified in the proposal.

proposer.text: The revision clarifies that while the logging feature automates storage, users must always provide and confirm the details before the logging is successful, therefore reducing ambiguity around expectations.

critic.text: The details in D2 clarify that users must provide details, but the requirement of confirming implies they might not retain input after the session ends.

tension.summary: The primary disagreement revolved around the handling of meeting logs when users leave the organization or change roles. The Proposer believes these issues are best addressed by establishing clear processes, while the Critic emphasizes the need for defined organizational policies to prevent loss of critical engagement history.

proposer.worry: The implemented process for capturing unlogged meetings may not be sufficient or reliable enough to prevent loss of crucial engagement history.

critic.worry: The logging process must remain consistently followed by users to avoid losing engagement history.

flags: Critic reported 85/100 confidence while blocker(s) C1 remain unsettled.
